correctness.rationale: The complete proof constructs the post-primary inhomogeneous two-state Markov reward system. Its backward difference w(t) is an explicitly positive integral, so expected repeat episodes conditional on primary-infection time strictly decrease. Transforming to cumulative exposure x yields F(q)=int(1-exp(-q x))mu(dx), a positive-measure Bernstein representation with strict derivative signs. The truncated-exponential likelihood-ratio order proves the strict upper ratio, and concavity proves the strict lower ratio. Known source final-size Q then yields explicit groupwise two-sided bounds. The argument holds for positive, integrable common force and the stated transient parameter regime. The accompanying standalone verify.py, actually executed from its packaged source, passed all six epidemic scenarios and source-count/conservation identities. Finite checks are ancillary and are not substituted for infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: Full published primary article §4.3 expressly leaves the separate leaky groupwise repeat counts unspecified and proves only a total. Earlier all-or-none equality is distinct; Edlefsen analyzes conditional initial-infection selection but not subsequent episodes. Prior vaccination and partial-immunity literature was compared by mathematical implication. The strict within-outbreak leaky reinfection-per-primary ordering, its computable two-sided subgroup bounds, and the complete fixed-pressure derivative hierarchy were not covered by the inspected scientific statements. Some older complete full texts remain inaccessible; priority is literature-bounded rather than certified.
residual_risks: The complete text of Gomes–White–Medley (2004) was not accessible; only its abstract and documented model contrasts were examined, so historical priority remains uncertain.
Katriel (2010) complete text was not obtained; its available abstract does not discuss vaccinated subgroup partitioning, but an earlier general statement could be relevant.
Complete text of the earliest September 2025 preprint version was unavailable; the complete 2026 published article was inspected, and priority to preprint-only variants remains possible.
An unindexed general Markov-reward or vaccine-effectiveness theorem may cover part of the fixed-force lemma; no universal uniqueness or independent validation is claimed.

value.rationale: The motivating article explicitly cannot disaggregate the cumulative leaky-vaccine reinfections that it can compute in total. The theorem supplies directly calculable strict upper/lower bounds on each otherwise uncomputed subgroup using only the paper's final pressure and inputs, distinguishes reinfection-share from primary-infection-share, and identifies a provable qualitative signature of leaky versus all-or-none protection despite identical post-infection susceptibility. The arbitrary-pressure Bernstein-response lemma shows the phenomenon is structural and not a tiny numerical example; the precise subgroup fact is motivated by the published unresolved epidemiological accounting problem. It does not claim vaccine effectiveness or an empirical clinical effect.
